<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915758_theRebbe_412" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915758_theRebbe_412__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This light above the chain of descent is drawn down through the self-sacrifice of Matisyahu and his sons, involving both an arousal from below and a drawing down from above, which explains the differences between the Chanukah lights and the Temple menorah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, this light</t>
    <t s="1">(which is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="2">that shines during the days of Chanukah and particularly in the Chanukah lights)</t>
    <t s="3">is drawn down through the self-sacrifice of Matisyahu and his sons.</t>
    <t s="4">That is to say,</t>
    <t s="5">the connection of this light with the darkness that existed then</t>
    <t s="6">is in two matters,</t>
    <t s="7">from below to above and from above to below.</t>
    <t s="8">From below to above,</t>
    <t s="9">that due to the greatness of the darkness that existed then, the power of self-sacrifice that is above the chain of descent within man was aroused within them,</t>
    <t s="10">and through this they drew down from the Essence of the Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent.</t>
    <t s="11">And from above to below,</t>
    <t s="12">that through this light they also illuminate the darkness.</t>
    <t s="13">And this is the reason for all the distinctions mentioned above between the Chanukah lights and the Temple lights,</t>
    <t s="14">for the light that shone in the Temple</t>
    <t s="15">(since its drawing down was not through self-sacrifice)</t>
    <t s="16">was a revelation of the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="17">seven lights.</t>
    <t s="18">And since the revelation of the chain of descent does not have the power to illuminate the darkness,</t>
    <t s="19">because the darkness is opposed to it,</t>
    <t s="20">therefore the place of the menorah was inside</t>
    <t s="21">(within the Sanctuary)</t>
    <t s="22">and on the right</t>
    <t s="23">(south),</t>
    <t s="24">and the time for lighting the lamps was during the period before sunset.</t>
    <t s="25">But the Chanukah lights</t>
    <t s="26">(which are after the self-sacrifice)</t>
    <t s="27">are eight lights,</t>
    <t s="28">a light that is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="29">which illuminates even the darkness.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The Rebbe explains why the Chanukah light is placed outside the door in the public domain, and questions why this was not instituted for Purim despite the self-sacrifice involved there as well.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And my father-in-law, the Rebbe, explains in the aforementioned continuation,</t>
    <t s="1">that therefore they instituted that the Chanukah light should be at the entrance of his house on the outside,</t>
    <t s="2">in the public domain,</t>
    <t s="3">even though we do not find a commandment</t>
    <t s="4">(aside from the Red Heifer)</t>
    <t s="5">that must be in the public domain,</t>
    <t s="6">because the purpose of the Chanukah lights is to illuminate the darkness of the public domain,</t>
    <t s="7">as above.</t>
    <t s="8">And at first glance,</t>
    <t s="9">this explanation requires further explanation.</t>
    <t s="10">For since the light above the chain of descent that shines on Chanukah</t>
    <t s="11">[and this light illuminates the darkness of the public domain]</t>
    <t s="12">is drawn down through the self-sacrifice of Matisyahu and his sons,</t>
    <t s="13">it would seem necessary to say,</t>
    <t s="14">that also through the self-sacrifice of Purim this light is drawn down</t>
    <t s="15">[and particularly since the self-sacrifice of Chanukah was</t>
    <t s="16">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="17">only in Matisyahu and his sons,</t>
    <t s="18">while the self-sacrifice of Purim was in all of Israel],</t>
    <t s="19">and nevertheless they did not institute on Purim a commandment that must be in the public domain,</t>
    <t s="20">only on Chanukah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Although the light in the Temple was also a revelation from above the chain of descent, relative to the Chanukah light it is considered within the chain of descent, requiring an explanation of the distinction between them.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, that the light that shone in the Temple was a revelation of the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="2">for which darkness is opposed to it</t>
    <t s="3">(as brought above from the discourses),</t>
    <t s="4">is relative to the light of Chanukah,</t>
    <t s="5">but in general,</t>
    <t s="6">even the light that shone in the Temple was a revelation above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="7">for which darkness is not opposed to it.</t>
    <t s="8">And as explained above</t>
    <t s="9">(in the discourse beginning "Padah b'Shalom")</t>
    <t s="10">that the building of the Holy Temple was specifically by Shlomo</t>
    <t s="11">(even though the design of the Temple was done by Dovid)</t>
    <t s="12">is as it is written,</t>
    <t s="13">"He</t>
    <t s="14">(Shlomo)</t>
    <t s="15">shall be a man of rest... and peace and quiet I will give to Israel in his days</t>
    <t s="16">(and therefore)</t>
    <t s="17">he shall build a house for My Name," etc.,</t>
    <t s="18">and that all the nations were subjugated to Shlomo</t>
    <t s="19">[which is why in his days there was peace and quiet]</t>
    <t s="20">is because Shlomo is the aspect of the King to whom peace belongs,</t>
    <t s="21">the Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="22">for in relation to this revelation</t>
    <t s="23">(which is above the chain of descent)</t>
    <t s="24">all opponents are nullified.</t>
    <t s="25">For this revelation</t>
    <t s="26">(that shone through Shlomo)</t>
    <t s="27">was also before the Holy Temple was built,</t>
    <t s="28">and in the Holy Temple this revelation shone even more.</t>
    <t s="29">Nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="30">relative to the revelation of Chanukah,</t>
    <t s="31">even the revelation that shone in the Holy Temple is included in the chain of descent.</t>
    <t s="32">And an explanation is needed regarding the distinction between the revelation of the Holy Temple and the revelation of Chanukah.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
